exposure: implementation of Interleukin 6 (IL-6) as an infection marker in clinical practice
outcome: antibiotic use in the first 72 hours of life
cohort: Very low birth weight newborns (VLBWN) born in the study hospital or admitted before 72 hours of life during two distinct two-year periods (2007-2008 and 2011-2012).
finding: The use of Interleukin 6 (IL-6) as an infection marker significantly reduced antibiotic therapy in very low birth weight infants during their first 72 hours of life without increasing mortality or other morbidities.
